## Purpose

Problem Set 2 asks students to *write* vectorized R code. But writing presupposes
being able to *read* — to look at a snippet, predict what kind of thing it
returns, and explain what it's doing. This worksheet is meant to be done
**away from a computer** — no running code, just reading and reasoning — so
every dataset it refers to is shown here, printed out, the way it would look
if you had typed it into the console yourself.

This worksheet selects six learning objectives from Pset 2 and, for each,
gives five snippets of increasing sophistication.

**How to use it:** for each snippet, fill in:

- **Type of result** — e.g. a single number, a logical vector, a character
  string, a data frame, a factor, `NA`, an error, etc.
- **Explanation of task** — one or two sentences on what the code is doing
  and why, in your own words.

Only after you've written both should you check yourself by running the
snippet.

Within each set of five, each snippet introduces exactly one new feature or
idiom beyond the last one. All snippets use only base R and the **dslabs**
`murders` dataset.

\snippetsep

## Objective D: Multi-category labeling with `ifelse`

::: {.keep}
**D.1**

```r
x <- c(-2, 0, 3, 5)
ifelse(x > 0, "positive", "not positive")
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**D.2**

```r
rate <- c(0.5, 2, 6, 10)
ifelse(rate > 5, "high", ifelse(rate > 1, "medium", "low"))
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**D.3**

A state's murder *rate* tells you how dangerous it is per capita, but
the *number of people affected* also depends on how large the state is.
Combine both:

```r
national_rate <- mean(murders$rate)
elevated <- murders$rate > national_rate
populous <- murders$population > 5000000
ifelse(elevated & populous, "Large & Elevated", "Other")
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**D.4**

```r
burden <- ifelse(elevated & populous, "Large & Elevated",
  ifelse(elevated & !populous, "Small & Elevated", "Typical"))
table(burden)
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**D.5**

```r
cut(murders$rate, breaks = c(-Inf, 1, 3, 5, Inf),
    labels = c("Very Safe", "Safe", "Moderate", "High Risk"))
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

## Objective E: Writing functions with conditionals and `NA` handling

::: {.keep}
**E.1**

```r
square <- function(x) x^2
square(4)
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**E.2**

```r
classify <- function(x) {
  if (x > 0) "positive" else "not positive"
}
classify(-3)
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**E.3**

```r
safe_sqrt <- function(x) {
  if (x < 0) return(NA)
  sqrt(x)
}
sapply(c(4, -1, 9), safe_sqrt)
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**E.4**

```r
harmonic_mean <- function(x) {
  if (any(x <= 0)) return(NA)
  length(x) / sum(1 / x)
}
harmonic_mean(c(1, 2, 4, 8))
harmonic_mean(c(1, -2, 4))
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::

\snippetsep

::: {.keep}
**E.5**

```r
classify_state <- function(name) {
  idx <- which(murders$state == name)
  if (length(idx) == 0) return("State not found")
  r <- murders$rate[idx]
  if (r < 1) "Very Safe"
  else if (r < 3) "Safe"
  else if (r < 5) "Moderate"
  else "High Risk"
}
sapply(c("Vermont", "NotAState"), classify_state)
```

\answerspace{Type of result:}{0.7cm}
\answerspace{Explanation of task:}{1.1cm}
:::
